Junk fees are hidden or unfair costs that too many companies – airlines, banks, hotels, ticket sellers – charge consumers. These fees may not matter to the very wealthy, but they add up and take real money out of the pockets of working families.

That’s why our Administration has been working to ban these fees and save families hundreds of dollars each year. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau took action to lower overdraft and credit card late fees, the Department of Transportation proposed a ban on family seating fees and required upfront disclosure of baggage and change fees, the Federal Communications Commission ensured consumers see upfront the full price and terms for their internet service, and the Federal Trade Commission banned hidden junk fees for live-event tickets and hotel bookings.

Collectively, the Biden-Harris Administration’s actions to cut junk fees will save Americans more than $20 billion a year. We were tired of the American people being played for suckers, and we took action.

President Biden believes no one should be jailed just for using or possessing marijuana. To help remedy our nation’s failed approach to marijuana, President Biden pardoned federal and D.C. simple marijuana possession offenses. President Biden also called on governors to issue similar pardons for state offenses. And, President Biden requested that the Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services review how marijuana is scheduled under federal law.

In May 2024, the Department of Justice and Department of Health and Human Services began the process to reschedule marijuana from a Schedule I to a Schedule III drug under federal law. Following the President’s lead, governors in Maryland, Massachusetts, and Oregon also issued pardons for some marijuana state offenses.

Far too many lives have been upended because of our nation’s failed approach to marijuana. President Biden took action to right those historic wrongs.
